evidence_excerpts: we express generalized identity with an operator, º, indexed by zero or more variables, which takes two open or closed sentences and yields another. Where p and q are open or closed sentences, (5) pºq should be read as 'For it to be the case that p is for it to be the case that q'.

we read such statements as not requiring that the flanking expressions be true/satisfied: for instance, it is intuitively no objection to (1) that there aren’t any bachelors. For short, we read them non-factively.
text: Generalized identity is a non-factive no-difference operator that can apply to factual and generic contents without requiring fact-shaped or property-shaped entities as its relata.
